routes.description: Establish that materialist and non-theistic accounts leave the existence, unity, and ultimate origin of consciousness insufficiently explained, while an eternal conscious God provides a coherent and comparatively simple ground for embodied human consciousness.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if consciousness requires an ultimate explanation beyond physical description, the non-theistic panpsychist alternative does not supply that explanation, and divine consciousness makes finite human consciousness more intelligible without competing with scientific mechanisms.

motionBridge.description: Consciousness points to God if divine consciousness supplies a better ultimate ground for human conscious experience than the available non-theistic framework.

centralBridges.description: The route must show that neural correlation and physical mechanism do not exhaust the reality or causal significance of conscious experience.
The route must identify why fundamental consciousness within nature leaves unresolved its origin or the emergence of unified complex minds.
The route must explain how an eternal conscious God can ground finite embodied consciousness and why this adds explanatory reach.

subsidiaryBridges.description: The route may support its account by showing that nonphysical mental causation and mind-brain interaction are conceptually coherent.
The route may extend its account to the rational, existential, and relational character attributed to human consciousness.

routes.description: Establish that consciousness can be treated as a fundamental feature of matter within a parsimonious non-theistic panpsychism, while showing that positing God neither resolves consciousness's place in nature nor follows from remaining theoretical questions.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if panpsychism offers a coherent non-theistic alternative to materialism and dualism, its open combination questions do not confer support on theism, and adding God provides no necessary or distinctive explanation of consciousness within the world.

motionBridge.description: Consciousness does not point to God if a viable non-theistic panpsychism accommodates experience and the addition of God lacks distinctive explanatory necessity.

centralBridges.description: The route must establish that quantitative physical science describes behavior without fully disclosing matter's intrinsic qualitative nature.
The route must show how treating consciousness as matter's intrinsic nature unifies physical structure with experiential data without supernatural additions.
The route must show that unresolved origins or combination details do not establish God and that theism leaves the world-level placement problem open.

subsidiaryBridges.description: The route may compare the ontological and lawlike commitments of panpsychism, materialism, emergence, and substance dualism.
The route may defend panpsychism's viability by identifying principled avenues for explaining unified complex consciousness from simpler experience.

sections.title: Consciousness and the Limits of Materialist Explanation
sections.rationale: This issue establishes the shared explanandum and tests what follows from neural correlations, quantitative physical descriptions, first-person experience, and the claimed explanatory gap.

sections.title: Nonphysical Mind, Causation, and Emergence
sections.rationale: This issue compares whether dualist or emergent accounts can coherently relate mind and brain, and whether their causal and lawlike commitments resolve or preserve the central problem.

sections.title: Panpsychism as a Fundamental Account of Consciousness
sections.rationale: This issue examines the positive case for consciousness as matter's intrinsic nature and the competing contention that making consciousness fundamental still leaves its ultimate origin unexplained.

sections.title: Unity, Complexity, and the Combination Problem
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether simple forms of experience can yield unified human consciousness and how any remaining combination or emergence problem affects the rival explanatory routes.

sections.title: Divine Grounding, Explanatory Relevance, and Parsimony
sections.rationale: This issue tests the motion-level inference by comparing divine grounding with non-theistic panpsychism on ultimate origin, simplicity, explanatory scope, and consciousness's placement within nature.
